\section*{Course Description}

Selected topics including an introduction to descriptive statistics,
collecting and interpreting data, finite probability and logical reasoning.
Prerequisite: MTH 101 or a rating of 2 on the placement exam. Fulfills
general education perspectives requirement. 

Instructional methods will primarily consist of lectures, in-class
discussions, and projects. However other methods may be adopted according
to the particular needs of the class.

\section*{Course Materials }

\textbf{Textbook/WebAssign:} A \emph{WebAssign }account is required
for this course. To setup an account complete the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Go to the website \href{http://www.webassign.net/}{www.webassign.net}.
In the upper right corner is a gray box, \href{http://www.webassign.net/v4cgi/selfenroll/classkey.html}{$ \begin{array}{l} \includegraphics[height=14pt,keepaspectratio=true]{WebAssign_Enter_Class_Key.png}
\end{array}$}, click on it (alternatively click on the picture; it is a hyperlink).
\item Enter the code: the code: \fbox{\textbf{\secWebCode}} 
\item Follow the step-by-step instructions.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{WebAssign }is free for the first two weeks of class (until \formatdateny{3}{9}{2014}).
An electronic copy of the text \href{http://www.amazon.com/Mathematics-Practical-Odyssey-Seventh-Edition/dp/B0072G1BXU}{\emph{Mathematics, A practical Odyssey} \nth{7} edition ohnson, David B. and Thomas A. Mowry}
is included with every WebAssign account. If you prefer to buy a physical
text, first \uline{make certain that it comes with a }\emph{\uline{WebAssign
}}\uline{code}. 

\textbf{Calculator: }A scientific calculator is required for this
course. Graphing calculators such as the TI-83, TI-83+, and TI-84+
are allowed and supported. 

\section*{Grades}

Grades will be taken from homework/quizzes, 4 exams, and a Final Exam
as follows:\textbf{}\\
\textbf{Evaluation: }HW/Quizzes $=20\%$, Exams 1, 2, 3, 4$=15\%$
each; Final Exam $=20\%$.

\textbf{Grading scale: $\mbox{A}^{+}\geq98\%>\mbox{A}\geq95\%>\mbox{A}^{-}\geq90\%>\mbox{B}^{+}\geq88\%>\mbox{B}\geq85\%>\mbox{B}^{-}\geq80\%>\mbox{C}^{+}\geq78\%>\mbox{C}\geq75\%>\mbox{C}^{-}\geq70\%>\mbox{F}$}

\textbf{HW/Quizzes: }HW/Quizzes will consist of any graded assignment
which is not an exam. The majority of this grade will be from the
\emph{WebAssign }online HW, however it will also include in-class
quizzes and projects. Unless stated otherwise, each HW/quiz will be
of equal value. At least two of the lowest HW/quiz grades will be
dropped. \textbf{}\\
\textbf{Final Exam: }The final exam will be given in class on \secFinal;
see the exam schedule \href{http://www.mhu.edu/academics/course-catalog/exam-schedule}{www.mhu.edu/academics/course-catalog/exam-schedule}.
\emph{If beneficial, the final exam score will replace the lowest
exam score.}

\section*{Class Policies}

MHU policies regarding attendance, \uline{academic integrity}, grades,
and change of enrollment will be enforced. It is the student\textquoteright s
responsibility to be aware of these policies and of related deadlines
as well as any announcements or syllabus adjustments (written or oral)
made in class. Please see the student handbook for details, \href{http://www.mhu.edu/campus-life/student-handbook}{www.mhu.edu/campus-life/student-handbook}.
All Mars Hill University students are expected to conform to the following
code:

\begin{center}\textbf{Honor Code}\\
``We, the students of Mars Hill University, pledge ourselves to uphold
integrity, honesty, and academic responsibility in and out of the
classroom.''

\textbf{Honor Pledge}\\
``On my honor, I have neither given nor received any academic aid
or information that would violate the Honor Code of Mars Hill University.''\end{center}

\textbf{Attendance: }$2.5\%$ will be deducted from a student's final
grade for each absence over five. Leaving early will count as one
tardy, and three tardies will be counted as one absence. \uline{There
are no excused absences}. Classes missed for personal or school related
events, e.g., sports, band etc., are included in the five absences
which are not penalized. 

\textbf{Missed HW/quizzes: }There will be no make-ups for in-class
quizzes unless the class was missed for a University sponsored event,
and advance notice of the absence was given by the student. In this
case the assignment will be excused or a make-up will be given depending
on circumstances. Late take-home assignments will have 25\% deducted
for each day it is late.\\
\textbf{Missed exams: }If a student misses an exam for a verifiable
excuse, they should send me an e-mail \emph{as soon as possible }so
that a make-up can be arranged. Make-up exams may be significantly
more difficult. If you will be gone for any reason, it will be \emph{your
}responsibility to inform me at least a week in advance to schedule
to take the exam early. 

\textbf{\textit{\emph{Snow Policy}}}\textit{\emph{:}} If class is
canceled due to inclement weather, I will send an email to the class
via MHU Webmail.\textit{ It is your responsibility to check your MHU
email account regularly for announcements from the instructor.}

\textbf{Student support services: }If you need course adaptations
or accommodations for a documented disability please contact the \href{http://www.mhu.edu/campus-life/disability-services}{Disability Services}
(828)\,689-1410 and/or \href{http://www.mhu.edu/campus-life/student-services/student-support-services}{Student Support Services}
(828)\,689-1380. The \href{http://www.mhu.edu/campus-life/counseling-center}{Counseling Center}
(828)\,689-1196 provides confidential intakes and assessments, personal
counseling and referrals to appropriate resources to all enrolled
students on a walk-in or appointment basis. 

\textbf{Disclaimer: }While I do not foresee any significant changes
to the items in this syllabus during the semester, I reserve the right
to make appropriate changes. Students will be notified of any such
changes in writing.
